neighbours.label: the indirect object or article right after a send/request verb ('send me a…', 'request a…', 'email us…'), strongest in contact-us invitations where a message/copy noun comes next
fire: To book a table for the weekend, just send me a quick note.
Customers who lost their receipt can request a replacement at the desk.
When the parcel arrives, please send us a short confirmation.
For a printed catalogue, simply request a copy through the website.
Should the link stop working, send me an email and I will fix it.
Anyone interested in volunteering can send us a short letter.
Members may request a refund within thirty days of purchase.
Once you have chosen a colour, send me a text with your size.
quiet: To book a table for the weekend, my sister baked me a small cake.
Customers who lost their receipt can find a bench near the desk.
When the parcel arrives, the dog brings us a muddy stick.
For a printed catalogue, the designer chose a font from the archive.
Should the rain stop early, grandpa will build me a kite.
Anyone interested in gardening can grow a small lemon tree.
Members may park a bicycle behind the main building.
Once you have chosen a colour, the painter hands me a brush.

notes: Probe: 'please send me a message' 0.57, 'request a free copy' 0.66, 'email us your comments' 0.36, 'sent her mother a postcard' 0.28, 'threw me a towel' 0.04; but a contact-style sentence without the verb ('If you have any questions, please read…') reached 0.39 on ' any'. Near misses are other ditransitive or verb + article frames.
